claims: The comment claims '70 open items... 57 name no issue', which is not reproducible on this branch. Measuring via `python3 -c \"import yaml; r=yaml.safe_load(open('docs/roadmaps/roadmap.yaml')); items=[i for i in r.get('roadmap',[]) if i.get('status') in ('planned','inprogress')]; print(len(items), len([i for i in items if i.get('github_issue') is None]))\"` yields 72 open items and 59 with no issue.
The withheld-step comment claims 70 open items and 57 with no issue, but docs/roadmaps/roadmap.yaml actually has 72 open items and 59 with no issue.
Inaccurate CI measurement: the withheld-step comment claims 70 open items and 57 with no issue, but docs/roadmaps/roadmap.yaml actually has 72 open items and 59 with no issue.
Arm 1 omits `expect 1 CB-2114 Pass` to hide that CB-2114 actually fires `NO-ISSUE` for null github_issue, falsifying the preamble's claim that a defect proves the other rule is quiet.

Silent Bypass / CB-2115 Change: If all open items lack a `github_issue` (names_issues == 0) and no repo resolves, the preamble returns `Skip`. This bypasses CB-2112/CB-2114 (which should Fail with NO-ISSUE) and alters CB-2115's behavior to skip silently. Control scripts miss this because they pass `--github-snapshot`, bypassing `detect_github_repo` entirely.
Bypass token: if an attacker ensures no open items have a `github_issue` (`names_issues == 0`) and the origin remote is missing, the rules return Skip instead of failing for missing issues.
CB-2112 and CB-2114 silently return Skip instead of Fail when `names_issues == 0` and no repository resolves, completely bypassing invariant A and B/F1.

Spec Fidelity: CB-2112 invents the `!issue.in_universe()` clause (ISSUE-EXCLUDED finding) for issues labelled `no-roadmap`. The spec definition in goal-mode.md §7 is strictly 'every open item has a github_issue, open, whose number is the item's numeric tail', with no mention of this exclusion.

Mutant: Mutating `if tail == Some(n)` to `if tail == Some(n) || tail.is_none()` survives all tests and control arms because no test pairs an item ID that lacks a numeric tail (like 'EPIC') with an actual `github_issue`.
Dropping the `IssueAbsent` branch survives all tests in linkage_tests.rs and all 15 arms of ticket-release-control.sh, as neither tests an absent issue.
Spec violation (CB-2112): the rule invents an `ISSUE-EXCLUDED` clause (`!issue.in_universe()`) not mentioned in the specification for CB-2112.

Mutant: Dropping the `|| release.starts_with('V')` clause survives all tests in check_ticket_release_tests.rs and all 15 arms of ticket-release-control.sh, as no test or control arm pairs an item with a capital 'V'-prefixed release.

Spec Fidelity: CB-2114 checks `!snapshot.milestones.iter().any(|m| m.title == *release)` but ignores milestone state. It allows an open item to bind to a CLOSED milestone (a shipped release). While following 'its milestone exists' literally, it violates the concept of open items on shipped releases.
Mutant survival: dropping `|| release.starts_with('V')` survives all test cases and the 15-arm control script, as neither tests uppercase 'V'.
CB-2114 passes open items bound to a CLOSED milestone because it only checks `m.title == *release` and ignores `m.state`.
Spec violation (CB-2114): the check ignores `m.state` and accepts an open item mapped to a CLOSED (shipped) milestone.

consensus: 3/3 lanes returned FAIL (lane-reduce agreed=false: every non-PASS lane is dissent, so all three are in dissent[]). Reading dedup[] claim text across its 14 groups (dedup groups by [file,line], which splits one shared claim into several groups): TWO claims are made by two lanes at the SAME line - (1) linkage.rs:225, CB-2114 tests only `m.title == *release` and ignores milestone state, so an open item may bind to a CLOSED (shipped) milestone (lanes 2,3); (2) check_roadmap_inputs.rs:78, the shared preamble returns Skip rather than not_measured/Fail when `names_issues == 0` and no repository resolves, which lanes 2 and 3 call a bypass of invariants A and B/F1. THREE further claims are shared by two or three lanes at DIFFERENT cited lines, so dedup lists them as separate single-lane groups: the `|| release.starts_with('V')` clause is a mutant no test or control arm would catch (lane 1 at :128, lane 3 at :220); CB-2112 invents the ISSUE-EXCLUDED / `!issue.in_universe()` clause the spec does not name (lane 1 at :62, lane 3 at :110); and the withheld-step comment in .github/workflows/ci.yml claiming 70 open items / 57 naming no issue is not reproducible, all three lanes measuring 72 open and 59 with no issue (lane 1 at :45, lane 2 at :48, lane 3 at :148). Genuinely single-lane claims: a `tail == Some(n) || tail.is_none()` mutant at linkage.rs:69 (lane 1); dropping the IssueAbsent branch at linkage.rs:97 (lane 2); and ticket-release-control.sh:158, arm 1 asserting only CB-2112 and never proving CB-2114 quiet (lane 2). No lane returned PASS or do-not-implement-as-written; uncovered[] and partial_reasons[] are both empty.
open_questions: CITATION AUDIT (delegate, read-only, branch PMAT-724-cb2112-cb2114-ticket-release-rules @ 92eafba2d): linkage.rs is 258 lines, check_roadmap_inputs.rs 120, ticket-release-control.sh 285, ci.yml 359 - no citation runs past EOF, but several point at the wrong line. starts_with('V') is at linkage.rs:220 (lane 3 correct; lane 1's :128 is the IssueAbsent push). !issue.in_universe() is at linkage.rs:110 (lane 3 correct; lane 1's :62 is the TAIL-MISMATCH discriminant string). The milestone-title test is at linkage.rs:225 (lanes 2,3 correct; lane 1's :136 is not it). The names_issues==0 Skip is at check_roadmap_inputs.rs:77-79 (lanes 2,3 correct; lane 1's :56 is not it). The ci.yml withheld comment is at :147-149 (lane 3's :148 correct; lanes 1 and 2 cite :45 and :48, which are not it).

REFUTED BY GREP: lane 2's finding at linkage.rs:97 ('dropping the IssueAbsent branch survives all tests ... neither tests an absent issue') is FALSE - check_ticket_release_tests.rs:204 asserts c.message.contains("ISSUE-ABSENT") && c.message.contains("#1"). The IssueAbsent push is at linkage.rs:128, not :97. Fable should discard this finding.

WRONG TREE on the unanimous ci.yml finding: the comment at .github/workflows/ci.yml:147-149 scopes its measurement to MASTER ('at PMAT-724's measurement master has 70 open items, 0 carrying release:, and 0 whose numeric tail is an open issue (57 name no issue, 13 name #612)'). All three lanes measured the BRANCH's docs/roadmaps/roadmap.yaml. My measurement (python3+yaml, status not in completed/cancelled, matching is_open at src/services/work_sync/mod.rs:285-287): branch HEAD = 72 open / 59 no-issue / 13 #612 / 0 with release (equals the lanes' figure); git show master:docs/roadmaps/roadmap.yaml = 63 open / 50 no-issue / 13 #612 / 0 with release. The comment matches NEITHER tree today, but the lanes' counter-figure is not master's either - the finding is directionally right with grounding against the wrong tree. Fable must decide whether 70/57 was true of an earlier master.

CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTABLE: MilestoneSnapshot has a state: IssueState field (src/services/work_sync/mod.rs:87-90), so the lanes-2-and-3 claim that linkage.rs:225 ignores milestone state names an available field, not an imaginary one. Whether the spec requires an OPEN milestone is Fable's call (goal-mode.md 4.1/7).

PARTLY CONFIRMED, lane 2's control claim: scripts/ticket-release-control.sh arm 1 (lines 155-159) writes an item with github_issue null AND release 3.41.0, then asserts only `expect 1 CB-2112 Fail "NO-ISSUE" "PMAT-001"` - there is no assertion about CB-2114 in arm 1, and linkage.rs:191 shows CB-2114 has its own NO-ISSUE finding for exactly that input. The structural gap is real; lane 2's word 'hide' and its claim about a preamble promise are interpretation I did not verify. For contrast, arms 2/4/6 do assert both rules.

SANDBOX ESCAPE (writes=false): the shared checkout's git status --porcelain gained three untracked entries during the run, all timestamped 12:39 while the lanes ran - /home/noah/src/paiml-mcp-agent-toolkit/scratch (a 4,501,456-byte ELF executable), /home/noah/src/paiml-mcp-agent-toolkit/scratch.rs ('fn main() {}'), and /home/noah/src/paiml-mcp-agent-toolkit/scratch_test/ (contains docs/). HEAD was unchanged (92eafba2d before and after) and no tracked file was modified. A --sandbox lane is NOT jailed at repo_root. I left the debris in place rather than edit under repo_root - Fable should remove these three paths before any commit or ledger regeneration.

NOT RE-RUN by me (rule 6): the branch's three acceptance commands (cargo test --lib tests_ticket_release linkage_tests tests_roadmap_coherence; ticket-release-control.sh; roadmap-coherence-control.sh). No lane reported running them either - every mutant-survival finding carries grounding 'asserted' except lane 3's :220, labelled 'measured' with no command shown.
